clue.text: David Jenkins resolved to be hanged with it under one arm, said John Aubrey

definitions.text: David Jenkins resolved to be hanged with it under one arm, said John Aubrey

parts.words: David Jenkins resolved to be hanged with it under one arm, said John Aubrey
parts.note: Aubrey's Brief Lives tells of the royalist judge who vowed to go to the gallows carrying the Bible under one arm and the 1215 charter of English liberties under the other

explanation.walkthrough: A general-knowledge clue: the document the defiant judge meant to carry was England's great charter of 1215.
explanation.definitionFit: The royalist judge Jenkins said he would hang holding the Bible and England's founding charter of rights, as Aubrey records.

clue.text: Recitative from Lothario (so lyrical)

indicators.note: from says the answer is taken out of the run of letters in the words that follow

explanation.surface: A lyrical recitative sung by a stage seducer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lyrical' describes the kind of recitative meant: the letters run across 'Lothario' and 'so'.
explanation.definitionFit: In music this term names a melodic, song-like style of recitative, halfway towards an aria.

clue.text: William Hayley produced its advocate

parts.note: the poet Hayley is credited with a work whose title pairs the missing word with Advocate, a champion of the whole nation

explanation.definitionFit: The missing word completes the title associated with Hayley, describing a champion speaking for the country as a whole.

clue.text: Caprine souvenir for a nymph

parts.note: in myth the goat Amalthea's broken horn, overflowing with plenty, was given to the nymphs who nursed Zeus

explanation.definitionFit: The horn of plenty came from a goat, hence caprine, and was presented to a nymph in Greek myth.

clue.text: Ginsberg's actual lunch?

parts.note: Allen Ginsberg's collection is titled with the word for what actually exists followed by Sandwiches, a whimsical midday meal

explanation.definitionFit: Ginsberg's book of poems is called Reality Sandwiches, and the first word means what is actual.

clue.text: A corner of Baldwin's work

parts.note: James Baldwin's play is titled The ... Corner, so the missing word is the one that precedes corner

explanation.definitionFit: James Baldwin wrote the play The Amen Corner, named for the pew area of a church.

clue.text: Children's writer a calm sort of Gide?

parts.note: calm means cool, as in keeping one's head

indicators.note: sort of signals that the name Gide is to be rearranged into another form

explanation.surface: A children's author is likened to a placid version of the French novelist André Gide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges the French novelist's surname. The children's writer is Susan Coolidge, pen name of Sarah Chauncey Woolsey, author of What Katy Did.
explanation.definitionFit: Susan Coolidge was the pen name of the American author of the What Katy Did books for young readers.

clue.text: Poet gives weighty support to idle talk

indicators.note: in a down answer the supporting piece goes beneath, so this piece follows the other

parts.note: idle talk is chatter
a ton is a great weight, hence weighty

explanation.surface: A poet lends heavyweight backing to some gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'support to' places TON below CHATTER. Thomas Chatterton was the boy poet of the Rowley forgeries.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Chatterton was an eighteenth-century English poet who died at seventeen.

clue.text: A short while on the lake for Baal

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a short while
a loch is a Scottish lake

explanation.surface: A brief pause by the water for a pagan god.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' just means the lake piece comes next in an across entry. Baal and Moloch are both Canaanite gods, so one stands for the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Both were Canaanite deities denounced in the Old Testament, so one false god stands for another.

clue.text: Knut Hamsun's coach?

definitions.meaning: Knut Hamsun wrote a novel of this name, a love story
a light four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage of this name

explanation.definitionFit: Hamsun's 1898 novel bears this title, and it is also a low carriage for two passengers named after a queen.

clue.text: Repentant adulterer chronicled by Vansittart

definitions.meaning: the Arthurian knight who loved Guinevere and later did penance
Peter Vansittart wrote a novel named after this knight

explanation.definitionFit: Arthur's knight sinned with the queen and ended as a penitent hermit; Peter Vansittart's novel retells his story.

clue.text: Ours was staged by Wilder

parts.note: Thornton Wilder's play is titled Our ..., so the missing word follows ours

explanation.definitionFit: Thornton Wilder's play about Grover's Corners is titled Our Town.

clue.text: Plot airmen reworked for verse by Pudney

indicators.note: reworked tells us the letters of the two words are to be put into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A storyline about pilots is revised for a poem by John Pudney.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reworked' rearranges PLOT AIRMEN. John Pudney, the wartime poet, wrote a poem of this name.
explanation.definitionFit: A poem with this title, about the bouncing apparatus, appears in John Pudney's verse.

clue.text: Complex string-pulling by Maurice Baring

definitions.meaning: a children's game of making intricate figures with a loop of string between the fingers
Maurice Baring wrote a novel of this title

explanation.definitionFit: The fingers-and-loop game is a literal tangle of strings, and Baring's 1925 novel carries the same title.

clue.text: "Yet them nor peer nor prince can buy, / Till —— themselves do cry" (Campion)

definitions.text: "Yet them nor peer nor prince can buy, / Till —— themselves do cry" (Campion)

parts.words: "Yet them nor peer nor prince can buy, / Till —— themselves do cry" (Campion)
parts.note: Thomas Campion's song There is a garden in her face ends each stanza with the street-seller's cry of fruit ready to eat

explanation.definitionFit: Campion's lyric closes with the street hawkers' call announcing fruit fit for sale, here the lady's lips.

clue.text: Medusa offering first letter on account

indicators.note: in an across answer on puts this piece after the one it rests on

parts.note: aleph is the first letter of the Hebrew alphabet

explanation.surface: The Gorgon presents the opening letter of a bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Medusa' is not the Gorgon here but a jellyfish in its free-swimming form; acaleph is an old name for jellyfish.
explanation.definitionFit: Zoologists call the jellyfish stage a medusa, and acaleph is an old term for such a creature.

clue.text: Add glosses for article on new (and old) gallery

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
N, as in rock 'n' roll, is a shortened form of and
the Tate is the famous London art gallery

explanation.surface: Writing notes about an essay on a fresh and an aged art collection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' gives a second N, the short 'n' of rock 'n' roll. The Tate is London's national gallery of British and modern art.
explanation.definitionFit: To annotate a text is to supply explanatory notes, which is what glosses are.

clue.text: Horror is his domain and creed

definitions.text: Horror is his domain and creed

parts.words: Horror is his domain and creed
parts.note: one surname belongs to James the horror novelist and to Lord Edward of Cherbury, whose writings on religion founded English deism

explanation.definitionFit: James Herbert wrote horror novels, and Edward Herbert of Cherbury set out a deist creed.

clue.text: Room offered by Greene here

parts.note: Graham Greene's story is called The ... Room, so the missing word precedes room

explanation.definitionFit: Graham Greene's story The Basement Room was filmed as The Fallen Idol.

clue.text: Mittelholzer's moved among them

parts.note: the Guyanese novelist Edgar Mittelholzer wrote a book titled ... Move Among Them

explanation.definitionFit: Edgar Mittelholzer's novel is Shadows Move Among Them, so these dark shapes moved among them.

clue.text: Lady Penelope followed by two writers in spa

parts.note: a pen is a writing implement
a feather, as a quill, was used to write

explanation.surface: An aristocrat is trailed by a pair of authors at a resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writers' are writing tools, not authors. Lady Penelope Penfeather is a character in Scott's St Ronan's Well, set at a spa.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady Penelope Penfeather is the patroness of the spa in Walter Scott's novel St Ronan's Well.

clue.text: "— the bad, ay, and suspect the best" (Herrick)

definitions.text: "— the bad, ay, and suspect the best" (Herrick)

parts.words: "— the bad, ay, and suspect the best" (Herrick)
parts.note: Robert Herrick's line advises avoiding the wicked; the gap is the verb for keeping away

explanation.definitionFit: Herrick's line counsels avoiding bad people, and the missing verb means to keep clear of them.

clue.text: A cruel word from Dinah Maria Craik

definitions.text: A cruel word from Dinah Maria Craik

parts.words: A cruel word from Dinah Maria Craik
parts.note: Dinah Maria Craik wrote a story collection called The ... Word, and the missing adjective means harsh

explanation.definitionFit: Craik's collection is titled The Unkind Word, and the missing adjective means cruel.

clue.text: Literary all through, like Brighton Rock?

definitions.meaning: Brighton rock is a stick of seaside candy with the resort's name printed right through it

explanation.definitionFit: A learned person is well read, and seaside rock has words running through its whole length.

clue.text: Ancient German symbol concerning French one included

indicators.note: included says the French word goes inside the word for concerning

parts.note: re means concerning, about
un is French for one

explanation.surface: An old Germanic character about which a French person is brought in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'included' signals the container; 'Ancient German symbol' is fair because runes were the alphabet of the early Germanic peoples, not modern Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Runes were the letters of the old Germanic alphabet, carved as symbols.

clue.text: By-product of Huxley's 1936 essay?

parts.note: Aldous Huxley's 1936 essay collection is The Olive Tree; what the tree yields is pressed for cooking

explanation.definitionFit: Huxley's 1936 book was The Olive Tree, and the pressed fruit of that tree gives a cooking fat.

clue.text: Essay David's prophet seen in devotion at Hanukkah when

indicators.note: seen in says the answer appears within the run of letters in the words that follow

explanation.surface: A prophet glimpsed amid Jewish worship at the festival of lights.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'devotion at Hanukkah'. Nathan was the prophet who rebuked King David.
explanation.definitionFit: Nathan was the prophet at King David's court who rebuked him over Bathsheba.

clue.text: When 14, less mature, wore white for Housman

definitions.text: When 14, less mature, wore white for Housman

parts.words: When 14, less mature, wore white for Housman
parts.note: Housman's Loveliest of trees has the cherry, unripe and in blossom, wearing white at the spring festival season

explanation.definitionFit: In A Shropshire Lad the blossoming cherry stands wearing white for the Christian spring festival season.
